body.p: III. Remarks
A. Introduction
Claims 1-11 will remain pending after entry of the present paper. Claims 1-11 were

previously pending. No claims are canceled by the present paper, and no new claims are added. Claim 1 is amended as set forth above. No new matter is added by the amendments as support for all of the recited features is found in the original disclosure. Reconsideration of this application, in view of the foregoing amendments and the following remarks, is respectfully requested.
B. Claim Rejections - Double Patenting

Claims 1, 4, and 6-11 stand provisionally rejected on the ground of non-statutory double patenting as being unpatentable over claims 1-7, 10, 12 and 16-19 of U.S. Patent No. 11,890,136. Applicant acknowledges the provisional rejections with respect to claims 1, 4, and 6-11, and will substantively address any double patenting rejections remaining when the claims are otherwise in condition for allowance.
C. Claim Rejections - 35 U.S.C. § 103
Stigall, Dausch, and Wada

Claims 1-8 and 10-11 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as allegedly unpatentable over U.S. Publication No. 2015/0305710 to Stigall et al. ("Stigall"), in view of U.S. Publication No. 2014/0257105 to Dausch et al. ("Dausch"), and in further view of U.S. Publication No. 2011/0062824 to Wada et al. ("Wada"). Without conceding that the rejection is proper and in the interest of furthering prosecution, Applicant has amended independent claim 1 as set forth above. As described below, claims 1-8 and 10-11 are patentable over Stigall, Dausch, and Wada.
With respect to 35 U.S.C. § 103, the PTO provides in MPEP § 2142:
The examiner bears the initial burden of factually supporting any prima facie conclusion of obviousness. If the examiner does not
produce a prima facie case, the applicant is under no obligation to
submit secondary evidence to show nonobviousness.
In the present application, aprimafacie case of obviousness cannot be factually supported for at least the following reasons. 35 U.S.C. § 103 provides, in part, that:
"A patent may not be obtained . .. if the differences between the
claimed invention and the prior art are such that the SVG {EMBED HERE} 0.3070.527 SVG {EMBED HERE} 0.311.373 would have been obvious befo fective
med invention to a person having ordinary
skill in the art .. ." (emphasis added)

Thus, when evaluating a claim for determining obviousness, all limitations of the claim must be evaluated. Further, MPEP § 2143.03 states that "[a]ll words in a claim must be considered in judging the patentability of that claim against the prior art." Quoting In re Wilson, 424 F.2d 1382, 1385 (CCPA 1970).
With respect to amended independent claim 1, Stigall, Dausch, and Wada, even in

combination, do not disclose or suggest "An apparatus, comprising: an intravascular catheter or guidewire configured to obtain intravascular data from a blood vessel of a patient while positioned within the blood vessel, wherein the intravascular catheter or guidewire comprises: a first segment; a second segment; and a coating separate from and disposed outside of the first segment and the second segment, wherein the first segment and the second segment are physically distinct components such that the first segment and the second segment are coupled to one another to form a length of the intravascular catheter or guidewire, wherein the coating extends over a location where the physically distinct components are coupled to one another, wherein the location is where a proximal portion of the second segment is coupled to a distal portion of the first segment, wherein the coating forms a seal preventing fluid ingress, wherein the coating directly contacts an exterior surface of the first segment and an exterior surface of the second segment, wherein the coating comprises: a proximal boundary at the first segment; a distal boundary at the second segment; and a continuous length between the proximal boundary and the distal boundary, and wherein the continuous length overlaps the location where the proximal portion of the second segment is coupled to the distal portion of the first segment." (emphasis added).
In that regard, Stigall, Dausch, and Wada, alone or in combination, do not disclose or

suggest "wherein the first segment and the second segment are physically distinct components such that the first segment and the second segment are coupled to one another to form a length of the intravascular catheter or guidewire", "wherein the coating extends over a location where the physically distinct components are coupled to one another", and "wherein the location is where a proximal portion of the second segment is coupled to a distal portion of the first

segment", as recited (emphasis added). Accordingly, Stigall, Dausch, and Wada, even when combined, do not disclose or suggest all of the features of amended independent claim 1. A prima facie case of obviousness has therefore not been established with respect to claim 1. Applicant requests that the § 103 rejection of claim 1 be withdrawn.

Claims 2-8 and 10-11 depend from and add additional features to independent claim 1. As established above, Stigall, Dausch, and Wada, even when combined, do not disclose or suggest all of the features of claim 1, and therefore, claims 2-8 and 10-11 as well. Aprimafacie case of obviousness has not been established with respect to claims 2-8 and 10-11. Thus, Applicant requests that the § 103 rejection of claims 2-8 and 10-11 be withdrawn.
Stigall, Dausch, and Wada

Claim 9 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly unpatentable over Stigall, Dausch, and Wada. Claim 9 depends from, and adds additional features to, amended independent claim 1. As shown above, Stigall, Dausch, and Wada, even when combined, fail to disclose or suggest all of the features of amended independent claim 1, and therefore claims 9 as well. Therefore, a primafacie case of obviousness has not been established with regard to claim
9. Applicant requests that the § 103 rejection of claim 9 be withdrawn.
IV. Conclusion

It is believed that all matters set forth in the Office Action have been addressed and that all of the pending claims are in condition for allowance. Accordingly, issuance of a formal Notice of Allowance is respectfully requested.
